answer: Ridge-sampled identity slots. Each epoch, a public verifiable random function draws a sparse ridge of eligible registration slots from a large key space, and no one can predict the next ridge before the beacon fires. An agent must claim a slot whose key maps to the drawn raven set, proving work against the beacon output. Because the target shifts unpredictably, an attacker cannot precompute cheap identities and must spend fresh compute every epoch, while honest agents reuse a bridge key across epochs at near-zero marginal cost.
